To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of NADPH oxidase and superoxide production are increased in aortic tissue of SHR, which leads to an impairment of the nitrite oxide signal transduction cascade.
hypertension is associated with an upregulation and activation of the NAD(P) H oxidase in the vascular wall, which leads to an enhanced production of reactive oxygen species (ROS).

the vascular NAD(P)-oxidase subunit gp 91phox and the endothelial nitric oxide signal pathway are both upregulated in hypertension, leading to an increased production of O2- and a diminished vasorelaxation to NO.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of NAD(PH) oxidase in vascular diseases.
the role of the NAD(P) H-oxidase in the generation and release of reactive oxygen species in the vascular system and the impact of these processes on the endothelial function.
the role of NAD(P)(H) oxidase in hypertension and its role in vascular dysfunction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the upregulation of NAD(P)(H)-oxidases in hypertension is not the primary cause of hypertension but is rather a consequence of hypertension.
the increased expression of gp91phox in the aorta of SHRs is not the cause, but a consequence of the increased oxidative stress and the endothelial dysfunction in SHRs.
hypertension leads to an upregulation and activation of NAD(PH) oxidase in vascular smooth muscle cells and endothelial cells and this leads to increased O(2)(-).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the upregulation of gp91phox expression is associated with a downregulation of NO signal transducing pathway in SHR.
the vascular NAD(PH) oxidase is a key enzyme in the generation of reactive oxygen species and is upregulated in hypertension.
the upregulation of NAD(PH) oxidase and downregulation of NO signal transductions are the main causes of endothelial dysfunction in SHR15.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vascular NAD(P)(H) oxidases play a major role in the generation of reactive oxygen species and in the impairment of the endothelial nitric oxide signaling pathway in hypertension.
the vascular NAD(PH) oxidase subunit p91phox and the endothelial NO signal transduction are impaired in hypertension.

NAD(P) H oxidase is upregulated in the aorta of SHR15 and this upregulation may lead to an increase in vascular superoxide production, which in turn may be responsible for an impaired NO signal transduction in SHR15.
